summary: Simplified Multicast Forwarding (SMF) provides basic IP multicast forwarding for limited wireless mesh and mobile ad hoc networks, where efficient flooding is an acceptable design. It defines duplicate packet detection for IPv4 and IPv6 and optional reduced relay sets. It is experimental.

eli5.summary: In a crowd, you shout a message and each person repeats it once, ignoring repeats. That is the idea, with smart ways to cut how many people repeat.

subtitle: Basic multicast forwarding for wireless mesh and ad hoc networks, built on efficient flooding and duplicate detection.

tldr.problem: In dynamic wireless mesh and mobile ad hoc networks, maintaining traditional multicast forwarding trees is less effective than in wired networks, so a simple way to spread multicast traffic is needed.
tldr.mechanism: Every SMF router forwards each unique multicast packet, using duplicate packet detection to avoid loops. Optionally, a reduced relay set of selected routers does the forwarding instead of all of them.
tldr.outcome: SMF gives a best-effort multicast service inside one MANET routing domain, linked to other networks through border routers. The RFC is Experimental and leaves several border router issues open.

sections.title: Flooding as a Multicast Service
sections.content:
Simplified Multicast Forwarding (SMF) extends the efficient flooding used for routing control messages in mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs) to the data plane. It is a basic, best-effort multicast forwarding service constrained to a single MANET routing domain, and it is meant for cases where localized, efficient flooding is an acceptable design.

The RFC argues that traditional multicast trees are often less effective in dynamic wireless topologies because of reduced reliability and increased dynamics. A basic service that reaches all SMF routers can still suit multimedia streaming, group messaging, peer-to-peer middleware and multi-hop discovery or registration services.

The architecture has three parts: neighborhood discovery, relay set selection and the forwarding process. Classic Flooding (CF) is the simplest mode, where every SMF router forwards each received multicast packet exactly once. Duplicate detection is still required, and the RFC RECOMMENDS more efficient relay sets to reduce contention and congestion.
sections.eli5: When people keep moving around, drawing a fixed map of who passes messages to whom does not work well. It is simpler to have everyone pass the message on once.

sections.title: Forwarding Rules
sections.content:
SMF handles locally generated multicast packets, which may need a marking for duplicate detection, and inbound packets received on an interface. It must forward multicast packets that are not router-local or link-local for IPv6, and not in the local network control block. The SL-MANET-ROUTERS group contains all routers in an SMF domain.

The mandatory rules are:

  • Packets not addressed to a multicast address MUST NOT be forwarded.
  • Packets with TTL or hop limit of 1 or less MUST NOT be forwarded, and link-local multicast MUST NOT be forwarded.
  • Packets whose source address matches a local interface, or frames whose MAC source address matches the router, MUST NOT be forwarded.
  • Packets for which duplicate uniqueness cannot reasonably be ensured MUST NOT be forwarded.
  • The TTL or hop limit MUST be decremented by one before forwarding.

To resist a pre-play attack, where a copy with a reduced TTL arrives first and poisons the duplicate state, the RFC recommends caching the TTL with each duplicate entry and forwarding a later copy that has a larger TTL.
sections.eli5: The rules are like a playground game: do not pass along something that is not for the group, do not pass your own message back, and stop passing once the message has gone far enough.

sections.title: Duplicate Packet Detection
sections.content:
Because packets can come back through the same interface or arrive from several neighbors, SMF requires duplicate packet detection (DPD). Routers keep a history of recently processed packets long enough to span MAX_PACKET_LIFETIME. There are two approaches, and all routers in a deployment MUST use a common one for IPv6.

Identification-based DPD (I-DPD) uses packet headers. For IPv6 it can use fragment header fields, IPsec sequence numbers, or a new hop-by-hop option called SMF_DPD, whose option type is 00001000 (hex 8). The option can carry an optional TaggerId to tell apart multiple ingress border gateways. It adds 8 bytes in the simplest case.

Hash-based DPD (H-DPD) hashes the non-mutable header fields, options and data with SHA-1 to produce a 160-bit digest, not for cryptographic use but to detect repeats. For IPv6 an optional hash assist value in the SMF_DPD option avoids collisions. IPv4 has no such option, since IPv4 header options are less tractable for hosts, and the 16-bit IPv4 ID field cannot be relied on, so H-DPD is RECOMMENDED for ordinary IPv4 packets. I-DPD for IPv4 applies only to fragments and IPsec packets.
sections.eli5: Everyone keeps a short list of the messages they already passed on. If the same one shows up again, they know to skip it.

sections.title: Relay Set Selection
sections.content:
Instead of every router forwarding, SMF can use a reduced relay set, a subset of routers chosen to forward while keeping the network connected. SMF MUST support CF when no relay information is available, and MUST be able to change its forwarding rules as relay state changes.

Relay state can come from three sources: independent operation with NHDP (the MANET Neighborhood Discovery Protocol, RFC 6130) supplying neighbor information, a coexistent unicast MANET routing protocol that provides its own CDS, or cross-layer information from lower layers. When NHDP is used, SMF defines an SMF_TYPE Message TLV and an SMF_NBR_TYPE Address Block TLV to advertise which relay algorithm a router uses.

The appendices specify three algorithms: Essential Connected Dominating Set (E-CDS), Source-based Multipoint Relay (S-MPR) and Multipoint Relay CDS (MPR-CDS). The criteria for candidates include robustness to mobility, localized election, small relay sets and support for preference metrics.
sections.eli5: Instead of the whole crowd repeating the message, a few people are picked so that everyone can still hear it. The picks change as people walk around.

sections.title: Border Routers and Scoping
sections.content:
SMF is meant to run inside a domain, so a border router or proxy MUST be used to connect it to networks with other multicast routing such as PIM. Border routers decide which groups cross the boundary, enforce TTL or administrative scoping, mark ingressing packets for duplicate detection, and talk to exterior routing protocols. The RFC recommends an IGMP or MLD proxy so that only groups with members are injected, but leaves its specification out of scope.

For IPv6, the RFC recommends treating an SMF domain as a site-scoped multicast domain, keeping FF05::/16 inside it. Multiple border routers are described as beneficial for reliability but raise challenges, such as duplicate unmarked packets, and the RFC says this is presently beyond its scope.
sections.eli5: A border guard decides which messages are allowed to leave the crowd or enter it, and stamps them so nobody repeats them twice.

sections.title: Security and IANA Actions
sections.content:
The main threat is denial of service against duplicate detection. A malicious router that can preview packets, for instance with a directional antenna, can send a copy with a lowered TTL first, creating a duplicate entry that blocks the valid packet. Predictable sequence identifiers can also be spoofed. The RFC recommends caching TTL values and adding an internal, randomly seeded hash to the packet identifier. When NHDP is used, its security considerations also apply.

IANA allocated the IPv6 hop-by-hop option type, created a TaggerId Types registry, registered the well-known SL-MANET-ROUTERS multicast address (224.0.1.186 for IPv4), and created a Relay Algorithm ID registry for the two TLV types.
sections.eli5: A sneaky person could shout a spoiled copy of the message first, so others think they already heard it. Keeping track of how far each copy had left to travel helps defeat that.
